initiative.title: OpenAgents Desktop: your coding agents in one Mac window, in Coax
initiative.body: Owner's order: first the same Claude Agent SDK chat as openagents.com/chat, working locally on the user's own Claude Code login (milestone desk-local-chat). Then Codex beside it, sessions, and the room where the agents talk to each other.

milestones.title: Zeron's UI in Coax, pixel for pixel
milestones.body: Owner's direction (2026-10-29): the desktop app, and later the web app, moves off the HUD look to UI forked from Zeron (Rust/GPUI, MIT, by Wing). Coax components drawn on the GPU the way GPUI draws them (quads with radii, borders and shadows, glyph-atlas text), one component at a time, each matched pixel for pixel against a screenshot of Zeron.

milestones.title: First: the web chat, running on your own Claude
milestones.body: The owner's first goal. The same Claude Agent SDK chat as openagents.com/chat (conversations, model chips Haiku, Sonnet and Opus 5.5 defaulting to Opus, STOP, cost per turn), but in a Mac window, running the user's installed `claude` with the user's own Claude Code login. No API key, no OpenAgents account, nothing sent to our servers.

milestones.title: Codex beside Claude, one transcript
milestones.body: Codex through `codex app-server`, and both harnesses normalized into one event model so one transcript draws either.

milestones.title: Sessions: sidebar, tabs, approvals
milestones.body: Several sessions at once, Claude Code or Codex each, in folders, with the old app's layout cut to the basics.

milestones.title: Agents that talk to each other
milestones.body: A shared room: ask_agent, tell_agent, agents_list and room_read as MCP tools for both harnesses, every message visible, no courtesy loops, STOP cancels waiting asks.

milestones.title: Resume, settings and a signed app
milestones.body: Sessions survive a restart, settings persist, missing or logged-out CLIs get one-line help, and a notarized .app/.dmg is built from this Mac.

tasks.title: A new chat screen with Zeron's input bar, pixel for pixel
tasks.body:
A brand new chat screen in apps/openagents-desktop/, connected to nothing, whose composer is an exact match of Zeron's GPUI input bar (/Users/christopherdavid/work/zeron, its UI crate and default theme). GPUI-style primitives in Coax (rounded quad with border and shadow, glyph-atlas text in Zeron's font) drawn by the Metal host. Typing, backspace, caret and placeholder work; send does nothing. The app opens on this screen; the HUD chat, LAB and router stay in the tree but aren't shown.

Reference: a screenshot of a Zeron dev build at a known size and scale. The pre-nuke Zeron adaptation is at 0b401561a0^:apps/openagents/. Attribution: Based on Zeron by Wing, MIT.
acceptance: build.sh makes OpenAgents.app from a clean checkout and it opens on the new screen
A --shot of the empty chat at the reference size matches the Zeron screenshot in the composer region, with the measured difference reported
Typing into the composer shows the text and caret; backspace works; the placeholder shows when empty
coax test passes for every new .coax file

tasks.title: The composer edits text the way Zeron's does
tasks.body: Full text editing in the Zeron composer, at parity with Zeron's composer (crates/ui/src/composer.rs and the GPUI it uses): selection with Shift/Alt/Cmd arrows, click, drag, double-click word, triple-click all; word and line movement and deletion; typing or pasting over a selection replaces it; Cmd+A/C/X/V through NSPasteboard; Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z undo and redo with Zeron's coalescing; a standard menu bar (app menu with Quit; Edit with Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All); NSTextInputClient for IME marked text, accents and the emoji picker; multi-line paste. The selection highlight matches a Zeron render in colour and shape.
acceptance: coax test covers selection, undo/redo, replace-on-type and word boundaries, and passes
A --shot with keys or a drag shows a selection drawn like a Zeron render of the same text, with the measured difference reported
Copy and paste go through the real pasteboard in a scripted check
The Edit menu shows Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All, and each works
IME marked text works through NSTextInputClient

tasks.title: The transcript and tool calls, drawn the way Zeron draws them
tasks.body: The Zeron-fork chat screen shows a chat transcript with a demo conversation (static data, connected to nothing), drawn as Zeron's transcript draws it (crates/ui/src/transcript.rs, crates/ui/src/markdown/render.rs): user bubbles, assistant Markdown (paragraphs, inline code, lists, code blocks), the thinking chip, and the tool-call tree (the group header with its summary and chevron, the activity rail, each tool's icon, label, file badge and status: shell with output, read, edit with its diff, search, web fetch, running and failed calls), collapsed and expanded. The transcript scrolls with the wheel and trackpad, a click opens or closes a group or a call, transcript text selects and copies, and the composer stays at the bottom. The demo content comes from Zeron's own demo transcripts (crates/client/src/demo/transcripts.rs). Matched pixel for pixel against a render of Zeron itself.
acceptance: coax test covers the transcript layout and the Markdown parsing and passes
A --shot of the demo transcript, collapsed and expanded, matches a Zeron render of the same conversation, with the measured difference per region reported
Scrolling, opening and closing tool groups and calls, and selecting and copying transcript text work in scripted --do checks
build.sh passes and the app opens on the transcript with the composer at the bottom

tasks.title: Claude or Psionic: chat with our own gpt-oss-20b through the Responses API
tasks.body: A Claude | Psionic mode on the Zeron chat. Psionic chats with our own gpt-oss-20b through the Psionic Responses API (POST /v1/responses, streamed): the harness rides on the model chip as in Zeron (mark plus model), a conversation keeps its mode and an empty one can switch; Psionic's chips show gpt-oss-20b and effort Low/Medium/High, the access chip gates its tools (read file, list folder, run command). The streaming client, SSE reader and curl transport go in coax/lib/gateway/; the key comes from PSIONIC_API_KEY or ~/work/.secrets/psionic-responses.env, never an argument or a log. Multi-turn replays the prior output items; busy (503 worker_busy), context limit, unreachable and Stop are handled. The modes and each chip's choices are data a picker reads (zeron/modes.coax).
acceptance: coax test --library passes for the SSE reader, the transport and psionic.coax, whose recorded streams (no keys) map to transcript parts, replay, tool calls and the busy, context, unauthorized, cut and Stop paths
The mode chip matches Zeron's harness chip in a side-by-side render, with the measured difference reported
A --shot shows a Psionic turn with its reasoning, a follow-up that uses the prior turn, Stop mid-stream, and the busy and unreachable messages
A Claude Haiku turn still works after the change
build.sh passes

tasks.title: The Lab decides with our own Elephant: /v1/systemone on Psionic
tasks.body: The Lab returns in the Zeron UI as a mode beside Claude (and Psionic). Each Lab message goes first to our own Elephant, elephant-1 served by psionic-serve --elephant-gpu (Psionic chapter 16, /v1/systemone) on coderos-4080, through coax/lib/systemone's keyless Psionic door over an SSH tunnel, with the old router's five questions (agent, difficulty, effort, Claude model, local work) and the agents this app can run as choices. The decision shows as a Zeron group, 'Routed to Claude Code · Sonnet 5.5 · Medium · 1.8 s', opening to every distribution, the latency, usage and the served identity; then the chosen engine runs the message. Busy, deadline, refusal and unreachable servers are error chips that say why.
acceptance: coax test --library passes for lab.coax, screen.coax, claude.coax, tools.coax and coax/lib/systemone: the request body matches the router's questions, a recorded real Elephant response maps to the decision group, and 503, 524, 413, other refusals and an unreachable server map to error chips

Three live Lab messages of different kinds ('hi', 'fix the failing test in coax/web', 'explain MXFP4 briefly') are each routed by our Elephant with the latency shown, and the chosen engine answers (--shot PNGs)
Claude mode still works, Psionic routes run on the Psionic engine (Claude answers when it is unreachable), and build.sh passes
psionic-serve --elephant-gpu stays up on coderos-4080 (tmux) and the tunnel command and start command are documented in docs/desktop/coax-desktop.md

tasks.title: One RTX 4080, two models: the app swaps Elephant and gpt-oss-20b on demand
tasks.body: coderos-4080's 16 GiB card holds elephant-1 (the Lab's router) or gpt-oss-20b (Psionic), not both. A small always-on switch there (psionic/platform/gpu-switch.py, systemd user unit psionic-gpu-switch) owns the card: use elephant, use gptoss, status; it stops only the server it started, waits for the requested one to bind and reports loading, ready or failed with the reason. The app asks it before a Psionic turn or a Lab decision, shows 'Loading gpt-oss-20b on the RTX 4080… N s' while a swap runs and sends when ready; a Lab message routed to Psionic loads gpt-oss-20b after Elephant decides and keeps it until the next Lab message. The app starts and cleans up its own ssh tunnels; Elephant's door can point at this Mac (PSIONIC_SYSTEMONE_HOST=local) with no swap.
acceptance: coax test --library passes for gpu.coax, lab.coax and screen.coax: the switch's answers map to the loading chip with its seconds, ready sends, a failed load is an error chip (and a Psionic route falls back to Claude Code), Stop ends the wait
The switch runs on coderos-4080 as a systemd user unit, never runs both servers, never stops a process it didn't start, and survives a restart
Live on the GPU: a gpt-oss-20b Psionic turn with reasoning, a follow-up that uses it, a Lab message routed by Elephant, and swaps both ways with load times measured (--shot PNGs)
build.sh passes

tasks.title: Mac host: a window that draws Coax HUD output with Metal
tasks.body:
apps/openagents-desktop/: a thin AppKit app (1320x880, min 900x600, inset title bar). It calls a Coax app compiled to C each frame and draws its vertex buffer with a Metal port of the HUD shader (apps/openagents-web/ui.wgsl), using the iOS app's Metal host as the reference. Mouse, keys, text input, scroll and the clipboard reach the app the way host.js delivers them on the web.

Spec: docs/desktop/coax-desktop.md. The old GPUI app this follows is at 0b401561a0^:apps/openagents/ (feature inventory: docs/research/feature-inventory.md there). Product logic is Coax; the Swift host only does window, Metal, input and OS dialogs. Everything visible is drawn by Coax in the Zeron UI (apps/openagents-desktop/zeron/); no comments ship.
acceptance: A build script makes the .app from a clean checkout on this Mac
The window shows a HUD frame and text drawn by Coax at 60 fps on a Retina display
A headless capture of the window matches a committed golden
Typing into a Coax text field and pasting work

tasks.title: Engine: run the local claude CLI with the user's login
tasks.body:
A Coax engine (apps/openagents-desktop/zeron/claude.coax) that runs `claude` through coax/lib/agent/claude (stream-json, control protocol) and coax/platform/process-native.c, polled without blocking from the Zeron UI's frame loop, one long-lived session per conversation. The child gets the user's own environment and login (no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY injected, no OpenAgents credential); the PATH comes from the user's login shell so a Homebrew or ~/.local install is found. Its events fold into the Zeron transcript the way Zeron's harness does it (streaming Markdown and thinking, tool groups and chips with results and diffs, the working indicator, STOP).

tasks.title: The room in the engine
tasks.body:
An ordered log of agent-to-agent messages per window; ask_agent runs a turn in the other session and returns its final answer as the tool result; tell_agent queues for the next turn; an agent waiting on an ask can't be asked by the one it waits on; STOP cancels its asks. No hop limit by default; a user-set one is allowed.

tasks.title: Model, effort and access menus: Zeron's picker
tasks.body: The composer's chips open Zeron's real menus instead of cycling: the model chip its compact model picker (pickers.rs, pickers/compact.rs: the effort over the model's name, the glass effort slider, the list page with Back, provider tabs, search and rows), the access chip its access menu (the modes with descriptions and a check, Plan mode with its switch), as popover_card anchored to the chip. Keyboard as Zeron's (arrows, Enter, Escape, Home/End, Tab, type to filter), a press outside closes, hover and selected rows. The options are data per mode (a catalog: Claude's models and effort ladder from Zeron's model cache, Psionic's gpt-oss-20b and its efforts), so another engine plugs in as rows.
acceptance: coax test --library passes for picker.coax (keys, filter, slider, anchoring, pointer) and screen.coax (chips open the menus, picks change the chips)
--shot PNGs of the open model panel, model list and access menu beside Zeron's renders of the same state, with the measured differences reported
A live Claude turn whose model and effort were picked from the menus runs on them (the session records the model)
build.sh passes

tasks.title: Attachments the way Zeron does them
tasks.body: The paperclip opens an open panel; drops and pastes of files or images attach too. Each file is staged into the app's uploads folder as Zeron stages it ({id8}-{name}, 24 MB at most, Zeron's notices on failure) and shown as an inline chip (Image N or the file's name) that the caret steps over and Backspace takes whole. Sent, the bubble keeps the chips; Claude gets the labels, the attached-paths list and images up to 5 MB as base64 image blocks (an SDK helper writes them into the frame). Psionic, text only: text files inline, an image refused with a clear message (a hook other text-only engines call).
acceptance: coax test --library passes for attachments.coax (chips, prompt, media types, the text-only hook), the SDK's tests (an image block from bytes) and screen.coax (staging, failure notice, Psionic refusal)
--shot PNGs of the composer with an image and a text file attached and of the sent bubble beside Zeron's, with the measured differences reported
Live Claude turns answer about an attached image and an attached text file
build.sh passes

tasks.title: openagents.com/chat drawn with the Zeron components
tasks.body: The web /chat page draws everything with the Zeron/GPUI components the Mac app uses (composer, transcript, Markdown, tool chips, picker menus), moved to apps/shared/zeron/ so both apps load the same files, and drawn by Coax on WebGPU: a WGSL port of Zeron.metal and a glyph atlas rasterized in the browser from self-hosted Geist (OFL) and Zeron's icons. The API stays as it is: Haiku, Sonnet and Opus 5.5, no effort, no attachments (the paperclip is hidden), tools as tool chips. Desktop width gets Zeron's layout with the chat list; phones get no sideways scroll, 16 px gutters, a docked composer and the list one tap away. Signed out shows Log in (/login).
acceptance: The Mac app's --shot renders are byte-identical after the move to apps/shared/zeron/
/chat#demo against the Mac --shot of the same state, per region, with the numbers in docs/chat.md
